name: Honda Motor Co., Ltd.
one_line_reason: The market prices Honda as a car maker burning cash on EVs, while the motorcycle and finance arms (JPY 650bn of half-year profit) are not shown anywhere in the headline.
evidence: 6-K for H1 FY3/27 (Nov 2026): consolidated operating profit JPY648.7bn (+48%), motorcycle JPY439bn (+19%), financial services JPY211bn, automobile operating loss JPY5.7bn on JPY7.54tn revenue, i.e. cars earn nothing. FY3/26 had a first operating loss in decades (JPY-414bn) after JPY1.58tn of EV-related charges; FY3/27 guide JPY780bn still carries large EV losses. Only 3 analysts in the yfinance count and ADV is tiny in the US ADR; the stock is within 7% of its 3-year high, so the surface (EV write-offs) is what is priced, and nothing in the filings says motorcycle cash is trapped, though car losses and EV supplier compensation spend the same cash.
key_numbers: Mcap $43.7bn; moto op profit H1 JPY439bn; fin svcs JPY211bn; auto op loss JPY5.7bn; SOTP gap +57% (verified inputs); EV losses FY3/26 JPY1.58tn

name: Baidu, Inc.
one_line_reason: The market has looked and judged: search advertising is shrinking 22% a year as ByteDance and Alibaba take share, and the large cash pile is being spent on AI compute.
evidence: Q3 2026 release (6-K, 2026-11-16): online marketing revenue RMB11.9bn, -22% y/y and -9% q/q, now 48% of Baidu General Business versus 62% a year ago; GAAP operating income only RMB626m (2% margin); adjusted EBITDA RMB4.5bn. Total cash and investments RMB276.6bn is confirmed, but FY2025 free cash flow was -$2.16bn (EDGAR XBRL), capex tripled in 2026 per press reports, and a roughly $16bn impairment hit in Q4 2025 results (Feb 2026). AI Cloud Infra +94% y/y is real but small next to the ad decline; five straight quarters of falling revenue by Q2. The SOTP cash cushion is therefore a pile management is deploying, not a trapped asset, and the screen's EV of $122bn counts debt without the cash.
key_numbers: Mcap $23.6bn; cash+investments RMB276.6bn ($41bn) vs ~$15bn debt; ad revenue -22% y/y; FY25 FCF -$2.2bn; 1y -41%; fwd P/E 11.7

name: JD.com, Inc.
one_line_reason: A food-delivery price war against Meituan and Alibaba pushed group profit into a loss in Q4 2025 and masks a flat but profitable retail core; losses are now narrowing.
evidence: Q3 2026 release (6-K, 2026-11-17): revenue RMB309.6bn (+3.5%), group operating income RMB5.2bn, JD Retail operating income RMB15.1bn (vs RMB14.8bn a year ago, 5.8% margin), marketing expense -26% to RMB15.5bn as New Businesses spending narrowed 'significantly' y/y. Q4 2025 had been JD's first quarterly loss (-RMB2.7bn) in almost four years on delivery subsidies; regulators summoned the three platforms in 2025 and 2026 to stop 'disorderly competition'. FY2025 free cash flow fell to $1.6bn from $7.2bn and operating income to $0.4bn (EDGAR XBRL), so the screen's P/E of 10 on trailing earnings is not a clean base. The retail core is not growing (flat operating income), the market doubts that the delivery war ends and that management stops buying (CECONOMY for EUR1.34bn), and Chinese-ADR discount applies; the retail core itself is intact.
key_numbers: Mcap $33.7bn; JD Retail op inc RMB15.1bn/qtr; group op inc RMB5.2bn; marketing -26% y/y; FY25 FCF $1.6bn vs $7.2bn FY24; P/E 10 vs 29 10y median; 5y -69%
